system.name: Hindsight
system.one_liner: a distributed tracing system that retroactively and lazily assembles detailed traces only for requests that later prove interesting

content.subject: how a typical (eager) distributed tracing framework tags, propagates, and immediately reports one request's trace data

elements.name: traceId / sampled
elements.role: the request-scoped ID and flag assigned at the origin and propagated with every hop

elements.name: traced process
elements.role: one of several processes the request visits; each records spans as small blue dots

elements.name: untouched process
elements.role: a process in the system that this particular request does not visit, drawn for topological context

elements.name: Backend Trace Collectors
elements.role: shared backend that ingests span data reported from every process

elements.name: Σ
elements.role: aggregation step that gathers the eagerly-reported spans belonging to one trace

elements.name: database
elements.role: persistent store holding the finished end-to-end trace objects

relations.what: the request continues hop to hop, carrying traceId and the sampled flag
eager trace reporting: every process reports its recorded spans immediately
aggregated spans are joined into one end-to-end trace object and stored

steps.what: a new request arrives and is assigned a traceId and a sampled flag
the traceId and sampled flag propagate with the request across inter-process communication
a component generates trace data (a span), annotated with the traceId
recorded span data is pulled out toward the reporting channel
eager trace reporting sends every recorded span immediately to the backend
spans belonging to the same trace are aggregated and joined into one end-to-end trace object
the finished trace object is stored

content.key_idea: A typical tracing framework tags a request once but then reports every span it generates immediately and unconditionally to the backend, win or lose, before it is even known whether the trace will matter.

summary: This figure walks through how a typical (eager) distributed tracing framework instruments one request. Numbered markers trace a request's wavy path through several system processes, shown as boxes containing rows of small blue dot icons for the spans recorded there, while other, untouched processes are drawn as empty gray boxes for context. At step 1 the request is assigned a traceId and a sampled flag; at step 2 these propagate with the request across inter-process communication; at step 3 a component generates trace data annotated with the traceId. Steps 4 and 5 pull each process's recorded spans out immediately ('eager trace reporting') into the Backend Trace Collectors, where step 6 aggregates and joins spans into one end-to-end trace object and step 7 stores it in a database. The paper contrasts this constant, eager per-span reporting with Hindsight's own lazy alternative, shown in the next figure.
summary_zh: 该图走读急切型追踪框架处理请求：①分配traceId/sampled→②随请求跨进程传播→③生成带traceId的span→④⑤各进程立即上报span给后端收集器→⑥聚合拼接为trace对象→⑦存入数据库，与Hindsight惰性方案对比。
notes: The given paragraph excerpts describe steps 1-3 in detail (traceId assignment, propagation, span generation) but do not narrate steps 4-7 explicitly; those are inferred from the caption ('eagerly ingested ... constructed ... processed, and stored') and the figure's own icons (Σ, join glyph, database cylinder). Process boxes are generic/unlabelled beyond their dot content, so they are described by role (traced vs. untouched) rather than individual names.
